items.title: GTFS Support
items.body:
# Backstory

Back in #699 @dnesbitt61 first suggested that we should add direct support for GTFS and outlined some of the steps to get there. Over the years a few different people have asked for such a feature and we even had a contributor who drafted #2835 but sadly was not able to get to the end.

# Current Status

At the moment we have what is quickly becoming vestigial transit routing support in valhalla. The code is not exorcised in CI, the core team does not administer any deployments that serve transit routes. At best we hope the code is still working but I suspect there are at least a few bugs to be squashed before we get it running again. Just today we had someone report in #3537 that our data tooling no longer works with the transitland APIs. This is the perfect opportunity to revive transit support in valhalla via directly ingesting GTFS feeds. Lets talk about our options.

# Proposal - Match the Existing Specs

The previous proposals for this support centered around transcoding transit data into a set of protobuf tiles (that match the geographic extents of our native transit tiles) as is done when interfacing with the transitland APIs. This approach has the benefit of using existing code paths and really becoming a project of simply converting from one format to another (though its not completely trivial). The concrete task list is as follows:

* gain access to GTFS data via bespoke or existing means (`just_gtfs` or `cgtfs`)
* support multiple feeds in an additive fashion
* avoid doing deduplication where feeds overlap geographies in the first pass we can save that for future work
* find a reasonable way to do association to the graph (finding the edges/nodes where to attach a stop/station)
* copy all of the required and optional data out of the feed according to the PBF spec
* data hacking where needed to extend schedules
* grab some utrecht transit to build with in CI so we can write tests on it (gurka support is unfortunately difficult at the moment)
* write some actual unit tests proving the algorithms still work with the data

# Specification

What follows is, based on looking at our proto specs and existing code a list of the various GTFS feed metadata and marking which we require, and which would be nice to have. Anything that is currently not used is not included in the list.

## agency.txt
| Field | Status |
| - | - |
|agency_id | required|
|agency_name |optional |
|agency_url | optional|

## stops.txt
| Field | Status |
| - | - |
|stop_id |required |
|stop_lat |required |
|stop_lon |required |
| location_type|required (generic nodes and boarding areas are not supported) |
| parent_station|required (for stops/platforms/ingress/egress located within stations) |
|stop_name |optional |
| stop_timezone|optional |
|wheelchair_boarding | optional|

## routes.txt
| Field | Status |
| - | - |
|route_id ||route_type |required | |
|route_type |required |
|route_short_name | optional (preferred)|
|route_long_name |optional (used only if no short name provided) |
|route_desc |optional |
|route_color |optional |
|route_text_color | optional|

## trips.txt
| Field | Status |
| - | - |
|route_id |required |
|service_id |required |
|trip_id |required |
|trip_headsign | optional|
|block_id |optional |
| shape_id|optional |
|wheelchair_accessible |optional |
|bikes_allowed |optional |


## stop_times.txt
| Field | Status |
| - | - |
|trip_id |required |
|arrival_time |required |
|departure_time |required |
|stop_id |required |
|stop_sequence | required|
|stop_headsign |optional |
|shape_dist_traveled |optional |
|timepoint |optional |

## calendar.txt (optional)
| Field | Status |
| - | - |
| ALL FIELDS | required (if applicable) |

## calendar_dates.txt (optional)
| Field | Status |
| - | - |
| ALL FIELDS | required (if applicable) |

## shapes.txt (optional)
| Field | Status |
| - | - |
|shape_id |required |
|shape_pt_lat |required |
|shape_pt_lon |required |
|shape_pt_sequence |optional (assumed sequential) |

## frequencies.txt (optional)

| - | - |

|end_time | required|
|headway_secs |required |

items.title: Cleanup vehicle types
Multimodal and wheelchair: GTFS wheelchair_boarding not considered for in-station transfers
items.body:
Hi,
I recently jumped into the multimodal routing algorithm, thanks to the new GTFS loader. Which works really great :+1: 

I'm mainly interested in wheelchair routing - currently working on a highly specialized custom costing, feeded with proprietary data. When playing around with multimodal routes, I realized that:

- `wheelchair_boarding` in GTFS stops is taken into account when transitioning from pedestrian to transit or the opposite: if the pedestrian costing `type` is `wheelchair`, the user won't be able to start or end a route from a stop without `wheelchair_boarding`
- This is not true for in-station transfers (changing trip at the same stop): the multimodal algorithm will happily ask the user to change bus in a stop without `wheelchair_boarding`. But in real life this would mean changing vehicle, so unboarding from the first one and boarding into the second one. Which sounds wrong if the stop os not `wheelchair_boarding` capable.

I realize multimodal + wheelchair is kinda dragon zone. So I first wanted to share my findings and the fix I did on my side to see if it sounds good to you. If so I'll be happy to try to write a test case and contribute a fix.

**What I found:**

GTFS `wheelchair_boarding` is set on transit stop nodes during transit ingestion:

 https://github.com/valhalla/valhalla/blob/c9c241873bab2155c814d5d04ab740f492427b06/src/mjolnir/ingest_transit.cc#L278-L279

This info will be translated into access mask on the hraph node during transit conversion:
https://github.com/valhalla/valhalla/blob/c9c241873bab2155c814d5d04ab740f492427b06/src/mjolnir/convert_transit.cc#L1061-L1063
and then
https://github.com/valhalla/valhalla/blob/c9c241873bab2155c814d5d04ab740f492427b06/src/mjolnir/convert_transit.cc#L593-L596

When connecting transit stops to the graph, new directed edges connected to this stop will inherit the access mask from the stop node:
https://github.com/valhalla/valhalla/blob/c9c241873bab2155c814d5d04ab740f492427b06/src/mjolnir/transitbuilder.cc#L233-L258

And finally, for some reason, access mask on the stop node in then reset (probably because this stop can be traversed on transit):
https://github.com/valhalla/valhalla/blob/c9c241873bab2155c814d5d04ab740f492427b06/src/mjolnir/transitbuilder.cc#L299-L300

So far, so good! A routing request with `"type":"wheelchair"` in pedestrian costing won't be able to walk those transfer edges, so no boarding / unboarding will be possible when transitioning from pedestrian graph to transit graph and vice versa.

But the multimodal algorithm, doesn't consider the pedestrian costing for in-station transfers: it just look for the next departure at this stop:
https://github.com/valhalla/valhalla/blob/c9c241873bab2155c814d5d04ab740f492427b06/src/thor/multimodal.cc#L391-L404
(the `tc->wheelchair()` here will be used to exclude if needed stop pairs from GTFS trips without `wheelchair_accessible`, which is not related to `wheelchair_boarding`.

**What I did:**

Don't reset access mask on the stop node, keep access mask inherited from `wheelchair_boarding`.
This doesn't break the transit costing because it does not evaluate access mask on nodes:
https://github.com/valhalla/valhalla/blob/c9c241873bab2155c814d5d04ab740f492427b06/src/sif/transitcost.cc#L560-L563

Then in multimodal algorithm, check access for the stop with **pedestrian costing** to check if boarding / unboarding is allowed for in-station transfers.

```cpp
            // In station transfer mean changing vehicle.
            // First check if pedestrian costing allow traversing this node:
            // Unboarding from the first vehicle, boarding in the second one
            if (!pc->Allowed(nodeinfo)) {
              continue;
            }
```

This work in my use case, but there might be unwanted side effects, and better options.

items.title: Consider kerb tags for routing
items.body:
Kerbs are quiet important for routing, especially for wheelchairs (https://wiki.openstreetmap.org/wiki/Key:kerb & https://wiki.openstreetmap.org/wiki/Tag%3Abarrier%3Dkerb). Currently valhalla doesn't respect any kerb tags at all. The height/type of the kerb plays a huge role if we want to allow access. 

For wheelchairs the tagging is quiet accurately defined here: https://wiki.openstreetmap.org/wiki/Key:kerb . For vehicles there might be some problems with kerbs. Even though the wiki hints about mistakes like not tagging e.g. highway crossings with `barrier=kerb`, its a quiet common tagging mistake (see https://overpass-turbo.eu/s/15C4 and https://github.com/Project-OSRM/osrm-backend/issues/5996). This is might lead to cars not being routed over normal highways if kerbs are dissallowed.

More specifically at `"heading": ,` which makes `response.json()` fail and I doubt is a desired return from Valhalla?

Claude suggested this could be due to the recent Rapidjson migration.
Here's his take on it:
```
Valhalla computes heading as a C++ double from edge geometry (essentially atan2 on the shape points). On a degenerate edge — zero-length segment, or percent_along: 0.0 where both endpoints coincide — that computation yields NaN.

RapidJSON is the link. The JSON spec forbids NaN/Infinity as number literals, so any serializer has to make a choice when it encounters one:

Library	             Behavior on NaN
Python json	         raises ValueError
nlohmann/json	     raises exception
RapidJSON (default)  writes nothing — empty token

RapidJSON's Writer::Double() calls its internal dtoa; when the value is NaN, the internal buffer is left empty and it writes the surrounding structure anyway, producing "heading":, — the key, the colon, nothing, the comma.

This wouldn't have surfaced before the 3.6.3 update if the previous Valhalla version either:

used a different serialization path that clamped or skipped NaN edges, or the specific degenerate edge type that triggers it was introduced or became reachable in 3.6.x geometry handling.
So the chain is: degenerate edge → NaN heading float → RapidJSON writes empty token → "heading":, in response body → json.JSONDecodeError in Python.

The regex fix (': null,') patches it at the Python boundary, but the root cause is upstream in Valhalla's geometry/RapidJSON layer.
Worth filing a Valhalla issue if you haven't — it's a straightforward guard (std::isnan(heading) ? 0.0 : heading) before the serialize call.
```

I don't have the call command, because it is deep within our system and only the error message bubbles up, but I figure the ids should be enough to fix the problem.

Good day to you!

items.title: MVT tiles contains wrong access attributes for backward edges
Introduce generic level change maneuver type
items.body:
# Issue

Valhalla currently produces instructions that prompt level changes only for a few types of edges (notably steps and escalators). These are not all the level changing linear features, though, and I think the user would benefit from having a generic level change instructions when there is a level change somewhere along the way (could be a ramp inside a parking garage, a wheelchair ramp, a bicycle ramp, or some other type of incline). Instead of having a fallback continue instruction, or even worse, having the maneuver be combined with whatever comes before, it would be more meaningful to communicate this level change in the broadest way possible (i.e. have a generic instruction that says "Move to level so and so"). 

This PR is an attempt at just that. This was fairly easy to implement, and I am open to discuss whether it would be better to simply identify all the other types of linear features that could change levels, but I feel like that might be easier said than done. We could always add more specific instructions in the future for different types of ramps, but this gives at least some base. Also, we would have to sacrifice some of the remaining values in `baldr::Use`, and since there are only a handful left, I wouldn't want to crowd them.

items.title: API design for bicycle types
items.body:
This issue is primarily to discuss if you would be open to having a more lenient API in the following case:
[bicicle costing](https://valhalla.github.io/valhalla/api/turn-by-turn/api-reference/#bicycle-costing-options) currently has the following types: `"Cross"`, `"Hybrid"`, ...
When returned from the API they are always lowercased `"cross"`, `"hybrid"`, ... 
Other costing models-types only accept lowercased input like pedestrian costing with `"blind"`,  `"wheelchair"`, `"foot"`.
=> Would you be open to a PR making `bike_type[0]=std::to_lower(bike_type[0])` and changing the logic downstream to only expect lowercased input?

items.title: Motorroad
items.body:
Fixes #855 
Motorroad logic only applies to road_class <= kPrimary.  If no override is found in the country access, we just use the defaults which removes bicycle, pedestrian, and wheelchair access unless a user entered access tags.  Otherwise, we will use the country access that is found in the db, but again unless a user entered access tags.  We never will change access if it entered by a user.  

At this point, only Spain has country access in the db that is different from the default (default = no bicycle, pedestrian, and wheelchair access; Spain = no pedestrian and wheelchair access.  bicycles are allowed)

Tested with EU and NA tests.  Added new tests for motorroad as well.
